title: Depending on other people
partialText:
In countries outside of the US, “libertarianism” is often synonymous with anarchy. In the US, it typically refers to folks who are really into unrestrained capitalism without the social support.
I was talking about this with a libertarian friend some time ago, and they said something along the lines of…
 What you’re describing means you’d have to really depend on other people.
 They meant it in a bad way.

title: Abolish patents
partialText:
So many anarchist principles seems like they would “never work”… because they literally cannot under capitalism, but would work just fine under a different system.
One really good example of that is abolishing patents.
Patents are silly, actually A patent says a person or company legally owns “an idea” or way of doing things, and no one else can use that idea or approach for many years. If you think about it for a bit, that seems really silly, doesn’t it?

title: It's embarrassing
partialText:
I made another unhoused friend today.
Jon is a tattoo artist who suffered a chronic injury his thumb a year ago and can’t do his work anymore as a result. He only recently became homeless.
He told me the same thing I’ve heard from so many unhoused folks I’ve talked to over the last year.
 It’s embarrassing.
 And I always tell them some version of the same thing.

title: AI is fucking awful (the guide)
partialText:

title: The Best of Us
partialText:
I don’t particularly care for Dolly Parton’s music, but I loved Dolly Parton.
She was literally the best of us.
 Unapologetically herself whether people liked it or not. Did not give a single fuck about what was “expected” of her based on her age, gender, career aspirations, and so on. Could have been a billionaire, but chose to invest tremendous amounts of money in communities that were underserved instead. A highly visible counter-argument to the idea that older white cishetero folks can’t help being racist, sexist, and homophobic because of when and where they grew up.

title: Make Care Visible
partialText:
There’s a rather popular flavor of social media content focused on helping unhoused people.
The creator will give out sleeping bags, socks, and care kits; sit down and have a meal; or take the unhoused person shopping. Sometimes they help them find work or start a GoFundMe to get them off the streets.
It does a lot of good. But it’s also gross AF! Imagine you’re cold, hungry, and desperate, and someone offers to get you all the things you need… if you consent to having a camera shoved in your face and the footage of you at your lowest blasted on the internet.

title: How to apply CSS only if there are a certain number of nested elements
partialText:
This week, I had to write CSS for a design where a list of elements got a bit of extra design treatment if there were at least three nested items inside it.
<!-- Base design --> <ul class="magic-list"> <li>Item 1</li> <li>Item 2</li> </ul> <!-- Extra design --> <ul class="magic-list"> <li>Item 1</li> <li>Item 2</li> <li>Item 3</li> <li>Item 4</li> <!-- ... --> </ul> I really wanted to avoid using JavaScript to add/remove an extra class, and the the :has() pseudo-class and the nth-* pseudo-class made it shockingly easy!
